title: Habitual grace in the soul's essence: Ferry admits it
source_text: XVIII. An autem praeter habitus virtutum detur gratia quaedam habitualis immediate ipsam animae essentiam penetrans atque afficiens, ut ex Scholasticis multi opinantur, res est de qua expresse non agunt plerique Scholae Reformatae doctores, sed a qua non multum abesse videtur, esse illud novum & supernaturale, & habitualis omnium facultatum innovatio, quam in regeneratione homini tribui agnoscunt. Paulus tamen Ferrius Pastor Ecclesiae Metensis nuper in Domino defunctus diserte ejusmodi quandam gratiam admittit. Et censet ante ipsum conversionis actum, a Deo in ipsam substantiam animae infundi habitualem quandam gratiam, quae totam animam instar spiritualis cujusdam lucis penetrat, & ex animae substantia in omnes ejus facultates sese insinuat: Et sic eas praeparat ut ductum gratiae efficacis sequantur, eique facile & sponte pareant, ut videre est in homilia illa quam publice edidit in Heb. 12. 28. Verum hanc sententiam pluribus scio non placere.
pass_a_gloss: XVIII. But whether besides the habits of the virtues there is given a certain habitual grace immediately penetrating and affecting the very essence of the soul, as many of the Scholastics opine, is a matter of which most doctors of the Reformed School do not expressly treat, but from which that new and supernatural being, and habitual innovation of all the faculties, which they acknowledge is bestowed on man in regeneration, seems not to be far distant. Paul Ferry however Pastor of the Church of Metz lately deceased in the Lord expressly admits a certain grace of this kind. And he thinks that before the very act of conversion, a certain habitual grace is infused by God into the very substance of the soul, which penetrates the whole soul like a certain spiritual light, and from the substance of the soul insinuates itself into all its faculties: And thus prepares them that they follow the leading of efficacious grace, and obey it easily and spontaneously, as is to be seen in that homily which he published publicly on Heb. 12. 28. But I know that this opinion does not please many.
pass_b_english: Thesis XVIII. Many scholastics hold that, besides the habits of the virtues, there is a habitual grace that directly penetrates and affects the very essence of the soul. Most doctors of the Reformed school do not deal with this question explicitly. Yet it seems not far from what they do acknowledge, namely the new and supernatural being and the habitual renewal of all the faculties that are given to a person in regeneration.

Paul Ferry, however, pastor of the church at Metz, who recently died in the Lord, explicitly admits a grace of this kind. He holds that before the act of conversion itself God infuses into the very substance of the soul a habitual grace. It pervades the whole soul like a spiritual light and from the soul's substance works its way into all its faculties.

In this way it prepares them to follow the leading of efficacious grace and to obey it readily and willingly, as can be seen in the homily on Hebrews 12:28 that he published. But I know that many people dislike this view.
